newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court allows VAT refunds on bad debt for money or barter.
newsitem.headline: Court allows VAT refunds on bad debt for money or barter.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday the VAT directive does not permit member states to refuse tax refunds for unfulfilled contracts because the consideration was in services and not in money.

The court refused to limit the effect of this judgment and said that member states which did not refund VAT on unfulfilled barter contracts since the Sixth VAT direcive was enacted in 1977 are subject to back claims by taxpayers.
The British tax authorities refused a VAT refund to Goldsmiths Jewellers who deducted 20,000 pounds sterling for VAT on advertising services which were contracted for but not delivered.

The British tax authorities argued the refund of VAT in case of bad debt is subject to the condition that goods or services are supplied for money because a greater risk of tax evasion exists if an unpaid contract is expressed in anything other than money.

The court did not accept that reasoning and said previous case-law holds that measures intended to prevent tax evasion cannot derogate from VAT rules, except within very strict limits demonstrated as necessary to acheive that aim.
The court stated that legislation altering VAT refund rules for all transactions not paid in money goes beyond what is strictly necessary to prevent tax evasion.
The VAT directive treats money and consideration in kind the same for VAT refund purposes, as long as the consideration in kind can be expressed in money terms, the court said.

"A distinction of the kind made by the legislation at issue discourages traders from entering into barter contracts, although such contracts are not, in financial or commercial terms, in any way different from transactions in which the consideration is expressed in money, and consequently restricts traders' freedom to choose the contract which they consider to be most suited to satisfying their economic interests," the court said.
Reference for a preliminary ruling by the Value Added Tax Tribunal, Manchester Tribunal Centre (United Kingdom) between

on the interpretation of article 11C(1) of the Sixth Council direcitve (77/388/EEC) on the harmonization of the laws of member states relating to turnover taxes - Common basis of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1)

On a proper construction, the derogation provided in the second subparagraph of article 11C(1) of the the Sixth Council directive (77/388/EEC) on the harmonization of the laws of member states relating to turnover taxes - Common basis of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment - does not authorize a member state which enacts provisions for the refund of VAT in the case of total or partial non-payment of the consideration to refuse that refund where the unpaid consideration is in kind, when it permits a refund where the consideration is expressed in money.
